title: Short Stuff: Macadamia Nuts
summary: Short Stuff episode on macadamia nuts. The hosts explain that macadamia nuts are technically seeds, not true nuts, and trace their origin to Australia, where they were brought to Hawaii by William Purvis, who planted them on the Big Island as a windbreak. Macadamias became popular in the 1920s, and after a global coffee market collapse around 1900 (the transcript says "nine"), the Hawaiian Agricultural Experiment Station promoted macadamia farming with land subsidies and a five-year tax exemption; acreage grew from 423 acres in 1932 to over a thousand acres. They discuss cultivars and why Hawaii dominates production. The hosts cover why macadamias are expensive (dessert nut rather than commodity crop, roughly seven years before trees bear crop, labor shortages, pests, expensive Hawaiian land, demand outpacing supply, prices around 25 dollars a pound). Health points include monounsaturated fats, fiber, net carbs, and minerals like manganese and copper, with a caution about calorie density. A brief float-test factoid closes the episode.

segments.title: Introduction and macadamia nuts vs seeds
segments.summary: The hosts introduce macadamia nuts, note the hosts' fondness for them and their richness, and explain that macadamias are technically seeds rather than true nuts.

segments.title: Origin in Australia and arrival in Hawaii
segments.summary: Macadamias originated in Australia and were brought to Hawaii by William Purvis, who planted them on the Big Island partly as a windbreak. Trees take four to five years to bear nuts. Their popularity grew in the 1920s.

segments.title: Coffee collapse and Hawaii's macadamia expansion
segments.summary: A global coffee market collapse hurt Hawaii's economy. The Hawaiian Agricultural Experiment Station encouraged macadamia farming with land subsidies and a five-year tax exemption. Acreage grew from 423 acres in 1932 to over a thousand acres. The hosts discuss cultivars and why Hawaii's climate suits the crop.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short break before the discussion of market issues.

segments.title: Why macadamia nuts are expensive
segments.summary: Macadamias are considered a dessert nut rather than a commodity crop. Reasons for high prices include Hawaii's market dominance, roughly seven years (the hosts also say four to seven) before trees bear crops, labor shortages, invasive pests, expensive land, and demand outpacing supply, with prices around 25 dollars a pound. Macadamia crusted fish is discussed as a dish.

segments.title: Health benefits and nutrition
segments.summary: Macadamias are high in calories and fat but contain monounsaturated fats, fiber, and low net carbs, plus minerals such as manganese and copper. The hosts note they are filling, but caution against overeating. Chocolate-coated and spam-dusted varieties are mentioned.

segments.title: Float test and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts share a factoid that nuts with high oil content, like macadamias, float in water, then sign off.
